newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Latest census shows Sri Lanka has more elephants.
newsitem.headline: Latest census shows Sri Lanka has more elephants.

text.p: The latest census by the wildlife department has shown Sri Lanka's elephant population numbers more than 4,000, higher than a previous estimate of 2,500 to 3,000, the state-owned Daily News said on Thursday.

It quoted the Deputy Director of Wildlife Nandana Atapattu as saying the latest census was conducted more scientifically and was based on dung counts and field interviews with villagers in elephant populated areas.
The newspaper did not say when the census was conducted.
Atapattu was quoted as saying that radio collars were being fitted on elephants to keep an accurate count in future.
Sri Lanka's elephant population has been falling rapidly as the mammals' natural habitat is absorbed for agriculture.
Officials earlier said Sri Lanka now had 2,500 elephants, down from 12,000 in 1990.
Many elephants are shot by farmers. Some 100 elephants died in 1996 and around 110 in 1995, wildlife officials have said.
